symptoms: Leaf spots are long (up to 2 inches), narrow, rectangular and light tan.
Spots usually stay between the leaf veins, but can join together and kill whole leaves.
treatment: Foliar fungicides labelled for gray leaf spot are available.
prevention: Rotate crops and till: both reduce the survival of the fungus.

sources.title: Gray Leaf Spot of Corn, Crop Protection Network

symptoms: Leaf spots are long (1 to 6 inches) and elliptical.
Spots are grey-green at first, then turn pale grey or tan.
In moist conditions the spots look dirty grey from dark spores.
Whole leaves can die on badly blighted plants.
treatment: Foliar fungicides labelled for northern corn leaf blight can be used.
prevention: Grow resistant hybrids wherever the disease is a potential problem.
Rotate crops and reduce surface residue through tillage.
maize___Northern_leaf_blight.severity: Among the corn diseases causing the greatest yield losses in the northern United States.

symptoms: Pale flecks appear on the leaf surface.
The flecks develop into powdery, brick-red pustules that are oval or elongated.
Leaf tissue around the pustules may turn yellow or die.
treatment: Treatment is rarely needed: common rust is seldom a concern in hybrid corn.
maize___Common_rust.severity: Occurs every growing season but is seldom a concern in hybrid corn.
